record.paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of almost periodic functions
record.original_question: For an element of APr(R, C) with 1<r<2, determine what properties are preserved or created by differentiation and by integration. In other words, investigate the behavior of derivatives and antiderivatives within the APr scale.

evidence.quote: d) Investigate properties of the derivative or the integral of an element in APr.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and notation. For 1 ≤ r ≤ ∞, define the space AP_r(ℝ, ℂ) of almost periodic functions as follows. Let T denote the linear space of complex trigonometric polynomials on ℝ, i.e. finite sums of the form P(t) = Σ_{k=1}^N a_k e^{iλ_k t} with a_k ∈ ℂ and λ_k ∈ ℝ. For 1 ≤ r < ∞, equip T with the Minkowski (Marcinkiewicz) seminorm

  ‖P‖_r = ( limsup_{T→∞} (1/(2T)) ∫_{-T}^{T} |P(t)|^r dt )^{1/r},

and define AP_r(ℝ, ℂ) to be the completion of T with respect to ‖·‖_r. The spaces AP_r form a decreasing scale: AP_∞ ⊂ … ⊂ AP_2 ⊂ AP_r ⊂ AP_1 for r ≤ 2, and AP_2 coincides with the Besicovitch space B^2 (the largest scale element for which Parseval's identity holds).

For f ∈ AP_r(ℝ, ℂ) with Bohr–Fourier expansion f ∼ Σ_k a_k(f) e^{iλ_k(f) t}, a formal derivative is defined by f' ∼ Σ_k iλ_k(f) a_k(f) e^{iλ_k(f) t} (when this expression represents an element of some AP_s), and a formal antiderivative ("integral") F is any series F ∼ c + Σ_{λ_k ≠ 0} (a_k(f)/(iλ_k(f))) e^{iλ_k(f) t} (when it represents an element of some AP_s).

Problem. Fix 1 < r < 2. Determine, for a generic element f ∈ AP_r(ℝ, ℂ):

(a) under what conditions f is differentiable in the AP_s scale (i.e. when does the formal derivative belong to AP_s for some s, and for which s), and which properties of f are preserved or newly created by differentiation;

(b) under what conditions f admits an antiderivative in the AP_s scale, for which s ∈ [1, ∞] this antiderivative lies, and which properties of f are preserved or newly created by integration.

In particular, characterize the precise mapping properties of the differentiation and integration operators between the spaces AP_r for 1 < r < 2.
artifact.status_search_result: The AP_r scale (a completion of trigonometric polynomials in Marcinkiewicz/Minkowski seminorms, interpolating between absolutely convergent exponential series and Besicovitch's B^2) was introduced in a 2011 paper "A scale of almost periodic functions spaces". The behavior of differentiation and integration on this scale for 1 < r < 2 is posed as an open problem, and no subsequent literature located through search resolves the mapping properties of derivatives/antiderivatives between AP_r spaces for this range. Status appears open.

status_evidence.title: A scale of almost periodic functions spaces
status_evidence.snippet: A scale of almost periodic function spaces is constructed by completing trigonometric polynomials in Minkowski seminorms with indices between 1 and 2, ranging from absolutely convergent exponential series to Besicovitch's B^2.
status_evidence.claim: Defines the AP_r scale relevant to the problem.

status_evidence.title: Representation of quasi-periodic functions and Hausdorff-Young inequalities for Besicovitch almost periodic functions
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work extends Hausdorff–Young inequalities to Besicovitch almost periodic functions but does not resolve the derivative/antiderivative behavior in the AP_r scale for 1<r<2.
status_evidence.claim: Recent related work does not settle the question.
